slack_title: October baseline: how often coding agents choose Exa
slack_setup: We ran the 50-prompt set on Claude Code and Codex: 16 use cases, each asked as tool selection, head-to-head and build, with and without an instruction to research the options first, plus the 2 usability prompts.
slack_findings: Builds go to the model provider's own search. Agents wire the search they can test with the key they already have. Exa was the main search in 4 of 64 builds.
In tool selection, agents mostly don't consider Exa. Losing agents opened an Exa page in only 4 of 54 cases.

Head-to-head losses happen after agents read Exa's docs (22 of 33). They pick a rival on one narrow need: exact-phrase matching, a total token budget, a news mode, or a source and price for each result.
Exa won every head-to-head on company, people and topic discovery. Leaving out places, events and funding, it wins 58%.
slack_next: Next month we rerun the same prompts and report these three numbers against this baseline, plus how often agents open an Exa page, since that moves before wins do. Each agent answers each prompt once, so we treat moves of 15 points or more as real.
slack_models: Claude Code on its default model (Opus 5.5) and Codex on its default (GPT-6.1 Sol).
